A.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, determine which represented billed revenue is associated with counterparties whose active contracts contain acquisition-relevant conditions, and report each qualifying invoice with counterparty and contract identifiers as they appear in the sources.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
entity_kinds: counterparties (as named in billing and contracts)
contractual terms bearing on change of control or assignment
exclusions: expired statements of work treated as inactive contracts for this purpose

world_eligible: invoice identity and billed name as recorded in billing sources
invoice amount, currency, billing period, and status as recorded
contract identity and counterparty naming as recorded in contract sources
contract active vs expired (including SOW expiry)
presence or absence of specific contractual clauses in source text (change-of-control consent/notice, change-of-control termination right, assignment consent/notice or restriction)
purpose_scoped: whether a clause counts as acquisition-relevant under Purpose A policy
whether a contract counts as active for exposure under Purpose A (expired SOW excluded)
whether an invoice qualifies for inclusion in the exposure report
whether invoice billed name and contract counterparty are confidently associated (asserted) vs not (unresolved)

epistemic_requirements: Ground assertions in authoritative source files; do not infer beyond what sources support.
Report invoice-to-contract association as asserted only when billed name and contract counterparty can be confidently associated.
Missing identity linkage is not a negative contractual finding: do not omit qualifying invoices solely because association is uncertain, and do not assert a join without confidence.
Use contract and counterparty identifiers exactly as they appear in sources.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: invoice is represented in output but invoice billed name and contract counterparty cannot be confidently linked

completeness_expectations.coverage: every invoice that qualifies under Purpose A policies must appear in invoices
completeness_expectations.qualification_rule: invoice is included when its associated (or candidate-associated) counterparty has an active contract containing at least one acquisition-relevant condition
completeness_expectations.identifier_fidelity: counterparty and contract identifiers must mirror source naming, not canonicalized aliases
non_goals: do not treat unresolved identity as proof of absence of exposure
do not suppress invoices solely because association is unresolved

acquisition_relevant_conditions: requires consent or notice on a change of control
permits termination upon a change of control
requires consent or notice before assignment, including assignment restricted except to affiliates or assignment prohibited to a competitor
purpose_specific_policies.active_contract_rule: an expired statement of work is not an active contract
purpose_specific_policies.association_threshold: asserted association requires confident linkage between billed name and contract counterparty; otherwise association must be unresolved
purpose_specific_policies.identity_policy: missing confident identity join is not a negative contractual finding

B.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, identify represented customer and commercial identities across CRM, billing, the company registry, and contracts, and report for each commercially relevant name or record whether it can be confidently treated as the same legal counterparty as other records or whether identification remains unresolved.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
universe_scope.record_scope: every commercially relevant name or record needed to connect CRM accounts, billed names, governing contracts, and candidate registry legal entities

required_output_shape.ordering: sort links by left ascending, then right ascending

world_eligible: CRM account records and identifiers as recorded
invoice billed names as recorded in billing
registry rows and company numbers as recorded
contract filenames and named counterparties as recorded
exact string equality or documented legal-form mechanical variants between source strings
purpose_scoped: whether two records are confidently the same legal counterparty (SAME_ENTITY)
whether two records are confidently not the same legal counterparty (DISTINCT)
which links are required to connect CRM, billing, contract, and registry candidates for a commercial relationship

epistemic_requirements: Do not globally merge records merely because names look similar.
Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be treated as mechanical equivalences.
Distinct registry entities with similar trade names are not automatically the same party.
Permit explicit unresolved identity; absence of a positive same-entity judgment is not a negative judgment.
Use the prescribed identifier forms for left and right endpoints.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: insufficient evidence to assert SAME_ENTITY or DISTINCT

completeness_expectations.coverage: include every link required to connect a CRM account, its billed name, the contract governing that relationship, and any registry row that is a candidate legal entity for that relationship
completeness_expectations.judgment_coverage: each included link must carry one of SAME_ENTITY, DISTINCT, or UNRESOLVED
non_goals: do not infer global entity canonicalization beyond required relationship links
do not default unresolved pairs to DISTINCT or SAME_ENTITY

purpose_specific_policies.similarity_rule: name similarity alone does not justify merge or SAME_ENTITY
purpose_specific_policies.mechanical_equivalence_rule: exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be reconciled mechanically
purpose_specific_policies.distinct_entity_rule: similar trade names across distinct registry entities do not imply sameness
purpose_specific_policies.negative_inference_rule: missing positive same-entity judgment must not be treated as DISTINCT
purpose_specific_policies.required_link_topology: links must span CRM, billing, contract, and registry candidate endpoints for each commercially relevant relationship

C.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, compute a commercial dependency view identifying counterparties that are commercially dependent under Purpose C rules, including open invoices and qualifying contract obligations, using Purpose B identifier forms.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
entity_kinds: contractual obligation kinds: exclusivity, auto-renewal, rolling term
universe_scope.temporal_scope: current commercial relationships only; expired contracts and closed historical one-off invoices without active contracts are out of scope for dependency

required_output_shape.obligation_kinds_ordering: sorted ascending within each dependency record

world_eligible: invoice open vs closed status as recorded
contract active vs expired as recorded or derivable from dates/terms in sources
presence of exclusivity, auto-renewal, or rolling-term language in contract text
which invoices reference which counterparties in billing sources
which contracts govern which counterparties in contract sources
purpose_scoped: whether a commercial relationship is current under Purpose C (open invoice or active auto-renewing/rolling contract)
whether a contract obligation kind triggers dependency under Purpose C
whether a counterparty-contract pair is reported as dependent vs unresolved
aggregation of open_invoice_ids and obligation_kinds per dependency row

epistemic_requirements: Identify counterparties using the same identifier forms as Purpose B.
If identity needed to join invoice and contract is unresolved, report the dependency as unresolved rather than as false (not dependent).
Ground contract obligation detection in authoritative contract sources.
Ground invoice openness and linkage in authoritative billing sources.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: dependency cannot be asserted because counterparty identity or invoice-contract join required by Purpose C remains unresolved

completeness_expectations.coverage: report each counterparty-contract dependency candidate that meets or may meet Purpose C criteria
completeness_expectations.dependency_assertion_rule: status dependent only when both current-relationship and obligation-kind predicates are confidently satisfied and identity joins are resolved
exclusion_rules: expired contracts do not create current dependency
a one-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not create current dependency
completeness_expectations.cross_purpose_dependency: relies on Purpose B identifier conventions and may inherit UNRESOLVED identity from reconciliation

current_relationship_requires_any_of: an active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term
obligation_requires_any_of: rolling term that continues unless notice is given
commercial_dependency_definition.conjunction: both current-relationship and obligation predicates must hold for status dependent

purpose_specific_policies.expired_contract_rule: expired contracts do not create current dependency
purpose_specific_policies.historical_invoice_rule: one-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not create current dependency
purpose_specific_policies.identity_join_policy: unresolved invoice-contract or counterparty identity forces status unresolved, not dependent false
purpose_specific_policies.identifier_policy: counterparty field uses Purpose B identifier forms (crm:, billing:, registry:, contract:)
